rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 <U+2014> the authors process 6614 DGA withdrawal records (filtered to 2779), join them with the water-rights cadastre, derive METRIC AET from Landsat (2019-2022) for 27 field sites and a 98.6 km2 AOI, and train a random forest to predict withdrawals from AET and rainfall (Fig. 10, Fig. 11).
rows.notes: The study does not test or report any result on using remote-sensed ET time series to dynamically adapt water allocations or to make the allocation system more resilient to seasonality or climate change. What it shows is a precondition: METRIC AET correlates moderately with reported withdrawals (R2 0.33, CCC 0.74; random forest R2 0.64), seasonal patterns of AET and withdrawals match at field and aggregated scale (Fig. 9, Figs. S5-S6), and AET plus distance-to-rights can rank auditing priority (Table 2). Linking this to adaptive allocation and resilience is proposed in the Discussion and Conclusions as a potential application, not demonstrated. Hence Q2 is no and the row is upstream.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 <U+2014> own processing of national withdrawal metering data, METRIC AET rasters from Landsat for 27 sites and a 98.6 km2 AOI, random forest prediction of withdrawals, and an auditing-priority raster (Fig. 10, Fig. 11, Fig. 12, Table 2).
rows.notes: No water conservation outcome (reduced withdrawals, water saved, improved efficiency attributable to remote sensing) is measured. The study reports that reported withdrawals are ~20-25% of granted rights, that AET correlates with withdrawals, that median field application efficiency computed from AET minus rainfall over withdrawals is ~80% (Fig. 11a), and that an auditing-priority map can be produced. Any conservation benefit of linking allocation to ET maps is suggested as a future application only. Q2 is therefore no; the result is upstream of the claimed effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a data-analysis/remote-sensing primary study in Chile; its results concern auditing and accounting potential of METRIC AET against metered withdrawals, not adaptive allocation, resilience, or water savings. Both claim rows cite it for effects it only proposes.
